title: Easy exam 7
about: Ten single-choice questions on the basics: one concept each, with the classic look-alike options.

options.t: The files that have at least the permissions `rw-r--r--`, even if they also have more.
options.why: That is `-perm -644`, with a minus sign before the mode.

options.t: The files that have any one of the permissions `rw-r--r--`.
options.why: That is `-perm /644`, with a slash before the mode.

options.t: The regular files whose permissions are exactly `rw-r--r--`.
options.why: A mode without a prefix must match exactly.

options.t: The regular files owned by the user called `644`.
options.why: The owner is selected with `-user`; `-perm` compares the permission bits.

questions.title: Numeric tests
questions.text: Which statement about `test` and `[ ]` is FALSE?

options.t: `[ 4 -le 4 ]` succeeds, with exit status 0, as 4 equals 4.
options.why: True: 4 is less than or equal to 4.

options.t: `[ 3 -ne 5 ]` succeeds, with exit status 0, as they differ.
options.why: True: 3 and 5 are different.

options.t: `[ 2 -gt 9 ]` fails, with exit status 1, as 2 is smaller.
options.why: True: 2 is not greater than 9.

options.t: `[ 10 -lt 9 ]` succeeds, since `10` sorts before `9`.
options.why: False: `-lt` compares numbers, and 10 is not smaller than 9, so the status is 1.

options.t: `bag`
options.why: The class `[^ae]` excludes `a` and `e`.

options.t: `beg`
options.why: The class `[^ae]` excludes `e` too.

options.t: `bug`
options.why: `u` is one character that is neither `a` nor `e`.

options.t: `bg`
options.why: The class needs one character between `b` and `g`; here there is none.

questions.title: The end of a log
questions.text: Which command shows the last 20 lines of `/var/log/syslog`?

options.t: `head -n 20 /var/log/syslog`
options.why: `head` shows the first lines, not the last ones.

options.t: `tail -n+20 /var/log/syslog`
options.why: That prints from line 20 to the end, however many lines that is.

options.t: `grep -c 20 /var/log/syslog`
options.why: It counts the lines that contain the text `20`.

options.t: `tail -n 20 /var/log/syslog`
options.why: `tail -n N` prints the last N lines, which is where the newest entries are.

options.t: `sed 's/-/+/g'` replaces all the dashes of every line.
options.why: True: the `g` flag means every occurrence in the line.

options.t: Without the `g` flag, `s/-/+/` replaces only the first dash of each line.
options.why: True.

options.t: `sed '/x/d'` prints the input without the lines that contain `x`.
options.why: True: `d` deletes the selected lines.

options.t: `sed 's/-/+/' file` changes the content of `file` itself.
options.why: False: it prints the result on stdout and leaves the file as it was; changing the file needs `-i`.

questions.title: Default permissions of new files
questions.text: Which command makes the new regular files created by the shell have the mode `rw-r-----` (640)?

options.t: `umask 022`
options.why: It leaves new files as `rw-r--r--` (644).

options.t: `umask 640`
options.why: The mask says what is removed: this one gives `-----w-rw-`.

options.t: `umask 027`
options.why: It removes nothing from the owner, `w` from the group and everything from the others: 666 becomes 640.

options.t: `umask 777`
options.why: It removes every permission: new files would have mode 000.

options.t: `ls` receives the text `*.txt` and searches for the matching files by itself.
options.why: The shell expands the pattern before `ls` starts.

options.t: The shell replaces `*.txt` with the names of the matching files and passes them to `ls`.
options.why: That is why `echo *.txt` shows the list of names.

options.t: In this pattern `*` matches exactly one character.
options.why: `*` matches any number of characters, including none; `?` is the one for exactly one.

options.t: The pattern `[!ab]*` matches names that start with `a` or `b`.
options.why: `[!ab]` is the opposite: a character that is not `a` or `b`.

questions.title: Optional letters
questions.text: `words` contains the lines `color`, `colour` and `colr`. What does `grep -E 'colou?r' words` print?

options.t: Only `colour`.
options.why: The `u` is optional, so `color` matches as well.

options.t: Only `color`.
options.why: `colour`, with the `u`, matches too.

options.t: The three lines.
options.why: `colr` has no `o` followed by `r`, so it does not match.

options.t: `color` and `colour`
options.why: `?` means zero or one occurrence of the preceding character.

options.t: `command > /dev/null` also hides the error messages of the command.
options.why: It discards stdout only; the errors need `2> /dev/null`.

options.t: Everything that is written to it is discarded.
options.why: It is the "black hole" used to throw away output that is not wanted.

options.t: It is a directory where deleted files are kept until they are removed for good.
options.why: It is a special file, not a trash directory.

options.t: What is written to it can be read later with `cat /dev/null`.
options.why: Reading it gives nothing: it stores no data.

questions.title: Daemons
questions.text: Which kind of process is a daemon?

options.t: An interactive process, because it is tied to the shell of a user.
options.why: Interactive processes belong to a shell, running in the foreground or background.

options.t: A batch process: it runs once, at the time it was scheduled.
options.why: Batch processes are planned for a given moment, like scripts launched on a schedule.

options.t: A background process that does a task of the system, such as a service.
options.why: Daemons work in the background for the system without being tied to a user's terminal.

options.t: A process that was suspended with Ctrl+Z.
options.why: That is a stopped job of a shell, not a daemon.
